      MAINSTREET, EXPLAINED

      A transparent treasury.
      Documented participation.

      A concept for a portfolio of business investments funded by actual trading fees.

      1. A company holds the investments

        It purchases eligible shares or other interests through the relevant provider. Investment documents establish what it owns.

      2. The holder’s rights are defined

        Exposure depends on enforceable rights in the investment company. Token balances alone do not create ownership of the underlying businesses.

      3. Cash and allocations stay visible

        Receipts, purchase costs, liabilities, valuation dates, and any distributions should be documented. Returns and liquidity are not guaranteed.

      This prototype has no issued token, live wallet integration, purchased business holdings, or confirmed Pons / Robinhood Chain integration. The business directory contains real external sources; model positions and account balances are fictional.

      DEMO MODEL TERMS

      What does 0.50% mean?

      In this example, a holder has an indirect 0.50% economic interest in the portfolio-holding entity. This is an illustrative assumption, not an issued entitlement.

      Investment cost
      $250,000 × 0.50% = $1,250
      Unallocated cash
      $18,750 × 0.50% = $93.75
      Model liabilities
      $0 assumed
      Distributions
      None recorded

      This model does not grant direct shares in the named businesses, voting rights, redemption, or a claim on treasury cash. Actual participation would require an appropriate structure and signed governing documents.

      The token-to-interest formula is not established. No token balance is being represented as legally backed equity.
